conviction_note: Mild negative lean: the one large new fact since Jumia last spoke (12 Aug) is Omdia's Q3 2026 Africa smartphone shipments -39% YoY (vs -7% in Q2, when Jumia's adjusted GMV still grew 23%), corroborated by Transsion's Q3 revenue -27%, which puts the Q3 GMV guide (15-25%) and the Q4 adj. EBITDA breakeven call at risk; but it is an industry proxy, management guided Q3 already expecting no chip relief, electronics is ~30% of GMV, the stock is already at a 52-week low (-15% over 20d, 11% below the August $5.52 placement), skew is near flat (+1.86) and short interest is modest, so p_up sits only slightly under 50 on a ~15% scale; impact_sum (-1.1) and the scaled number (-1.2) agree.
bar: GMV: company guide Q3 2026 GMV growth +15% to +25% YoY adjusted for perimeter (Algeria exit), FY2026 +20% to +30%; adj. EBITDA: FY2026 loss $25-30M with Q4 2026 breakeven, which with H1 loss $19.4M (Q1 $10.7M + Q2 $8.7M) implies a Q3 loss of roughly $5.6-10.6M (Q2 $8.7M, Q3 2025 $14.0M). Source: https://www.newswire.com/news/jumia-reports-second-quarter-2026-results-and-announces-capital-raise and https://www.newswire.com/news/jumia-reports-first-quarter-2026-results . Sell-side revenue/EPS bar is DISPUTED: Q3 revenue consensus $46.5M (Benzinga snapshot ~Oct 22) vs $56M (StockAlarm), EPS -$0.05 (EarningsWhispers) to -$0.07/-0.08 (TipRanks); revenue/EPS findings capped small for that reason. print_vs_bar_pct is measured on GMV against the guide midpoint (+20%).
positioning_check: Short interest modest and falling: ORTEX ~5.1% of free float, 3.6 days to cover, CTB 2.11% as of 2026-10-22 (https://app.ortex.com/s/NYSE/JMIA, via search snippet); ShortSqueeze ~4.52M shares, 2.8 days to cover dated 2026-11-09 (https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=JMIA); Equibles ~3.98% of float end-Sept. Not a crowded short. Options: 25d skew +1.86 vol pts (mild put premium, baseline calls it balanced), put/call OI 0.29 (call-heavy open interest), ATM IV 193%, event-implied move 15.62%. Tape: spot $4.915 at a 52-week low, -10.96% 5d, -15.11% 20d, -66% from 52w high. Documented seller: Pleasant Lake (Fund 1 Investments) cut from 7.48% to 4.5% over Q3 (13G/A filed 2026-11-16).

findings.finding: Omdia's Q3 2026 data (published 30 Oct, after Jumia last spoke on 12 Aug) has African smartphone shipments down 39% YoY, the steepest regional fall, against -7% in Q2 2026 when Jumia's perimeter-adjusted GMV still grew 23% and phones/electronics were already flagged as the drag; electronics is roughly 30% of Jumia GMV, so the Q3 15-25% GMV guide and the FY 20-30% guide (and by extension the Q4 adj. EBITDA breakeven message) are at risk of landing at the low end or being cut, net of ASP inflation and the 70% of GMV outside electronics (Nigeria +36% in Q2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline history empty (6-K history unreadable). From press: Q4 2025 print 2026-02-10 stock -17% intraday (https://www-web.itiger.com/news/2610678386); Q1 2026 print 2026-05-08 stock down ~11% (MarketBeat headline); Q2 2026 print 2026-08-12, when the FY GMV guide was CUT from 27-32% to 20-30% for chip shortages but a $50M IFC-led raise was announced, the stock rose ~7.7% (https://parameter.io/jumia-jmia-stock-surges-8-on-strong-q2-earnings-and-50m-funding-round/). So a guide cut alone has been absorbed once when paired with good news.
findings.why_not_priced: The Omdia regional figure was in secondary coverage of a global report, not in any Jumia preview found; sell-side revenue snapshots ($46.5M Benzinga, Oct) predate or ignore it. If it were fully priced the skew would be bid well above +1.86 and put OI would not be 0.29 of calls. Partly priced: the stock is -15% over 20 days and at a 52-week low since the data came out, which may already reflect it.
findings.independence: Transsion (Tecno/Infinix, ~47-51% Africa smartphone share, a direct supplier of phones sold on Jumia) Q3 2026 revenue -27.45% YoY, ASPs raised deliberately, inventory nearly doubled: https://tech-ish.com/2026/11/02/tecno-and-infinixs-parent-transsion-saw-third-quarter-revenue-fall-27-as-memory-costs-rose/ (2026-11-02). Company side: Q2 release said smartphone supply disruption would 'persist into early Q3' (https://www.newswire.com/news/jumia-reports-second-quarter-2026-results-and-announces-capital-raise), i.e. the guide assumed some of this. Proxy, not company-confirmed.

findings.finding: The naira held around N1,329/$ through September 2026 (official NFEM) against roughly N1,475-1,526/$ in September 2025, a ~10-13% YoY appreciation in Jumia's largest market, while the Egyptian pound weakened ~6% (EGP ~52/$ end-Sept 2026); net, USD-reported GMV/revenue gets an FX tailwind similar to Q2 (reported GMV +20% vs +15% constant currency).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean record of the stock reacting to FX tailwinds; Q2 2026's 5-point FX tailwind sat inside a print that rose ~7.7% mainly on the capital raise.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced and mostly inside the guide: the naira was already at similar levels when the Q3 guide was set on 12 Aug. Small residual because naira stability held through the whole quarter (longest stability since July 2025) rather than reversing.
findings.independence: September 2025 comparator: https://businessday.ng/markets/article/naira-loses-n9-88-to-dollar-amid-rising-external-reserves/ (N1,475.34 close 30 Sep 2025, BusinessDay citing CBN, via search); EGP: https://arabfinance.com/en/news/newdetails/usd-egp-exchange-rates-on-september-29 . Macro-to-company transmission, proxy.

findings.finding: Pleasant Lake Partners (Fund 1 Investments) cut its Jumia holding from 18,524,754 ordinary shares (7.48%) at 30 Jun 2026 to 12,016,198 (4.5%) at 30 Sep 2026 per a 13G/A filed 2026-11-16, despite receiving 2,536,230 shares in the 27 Aug placement at $5.52/ADS, i.e. it sold ~9M ordinary shares (~4.5M ADSs, ~3 days of ADS volume) in Q3 and is now below the 5% line, so further selling is invisible; its 1.27M placement ADSs are registered for resale (F-3ASR 2026-08-28) alongside Discovery Global, Cantor and Shay, and spot $4.915 is 11% under the $5.52 placement price.
findings.why_not_priced: Filed the day before the print and not in any wire copy found. Cuts both ways: it documents a supply overhang from a holder that has been distributing, but also offers a flow (not information) explanation for part of the -15% 20-day drawdown, which a clean print could reverse. Net sized near zero.
findings.independence: Prior 13G/A: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1756708/000092963826003081/primary_doc.xml (7.48% at 2026-06-30). Resale registration: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1756708/000121390026095022/ea0302527-f3asr_jumia.htm . Same filer family; no independent source.

findings.finding: Jumia has beaten sell-side revenue consensus by a wide margin two quarters running (Q1 2026 $50.6M vs $39.6M est; Q2 2026 $52.0M vs $45.8M est), and at least one Q3 revenue consensus snapshot ($46.5M, Benzinga ~Oct 22) sits below the Q2 run-rate, while another ($56M, StockAlarm) sits above it; Q3 2025 revenue was $45.6M, flat on Q2 2025.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have not been paid: Q1 2026 revenue beat by ~28% and the stock fell ~11%; Q3 2025 a headline 'revenue miss' was sold 5.4% pre-market (https://www.itiger.com/news/1128837078). The stock trades on GMV, EBITDA and the breakeven path, not revenue.

findings.why_not_priced: The bar itself is disputed between sources ($46.5M vs $56M), so a headline 'beat' or 'miss' depends on which a wire picks; capped small per the unresolved bar.
findings.independence: StockAlarm $56M (https://pro.stockalarm.io/quote/JMIA/analysts, search snippet only) disagrees; Q2 actual from company release https://www.newswire.com/news/jumia-reports-second-quarter-2026-results-and-announces-capital-raise .

findings.finding: The $50M private placement (IFC $25M, Axian and others; 9.1M ADSs at $5.52) closed: the F-3ASR filed 2026-08-28 states the purchase ADSs were issued on 27 Aug 2026, so Q3 liquidity should read about $48.3M (30 Jun) plus ~$50M less one quarter of burn (~$12-15M), removing funding risk ahead of the Q4 breakeven target; the money is for logistics, warehouses and JumiaPay, and the CEO said breakeven did not need it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The raise's announcement day (2026-08-12) the stock rose ~7.7% despite a GMV guide cut.
findings.why_not_priced: Known since August; little residual. Search coverage never reported the closing, so some holders may still carry funding risk, but the stock trading below the placement price says the raise is not supporting it.
findings.independence: CEO interview: https://group.jumia.com/news/jumia-de-risks-profitability-path-with-50m-ifc-deal-ceo-says-investingcom ('we can reach breakeven without additional cash').

baseline_tension: The negative lean agrees with the run-up (-15% 20d, 52-week low) and only weakly with the near-flat skew (+1.86), so much of it may already be in the price; the call-heavy OI (P/C 0.29) and the stock trading under the August placement price argue a non-catastrophic print could squeeze up, which is why p_up is held at 46 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (proxy) and rule 9 (segment net of the rest): Omdia/Transsion phone finding cut from -2.5 to -2.0, since it is an industry proxy on ~30% of GMV, the guide already assumed continued chip disruption, and the other ~70% (Nigeria +36% in Q2) has been growing.
Rule 5 (positioning is not an explanation by itself) and rule 3 (own caveat): Pleasant Lake selling finding cut from -0.3 to -0.2 because its own why_not_priced argues both directions.
Wire-copy rule: Cantor PT cut from +0.2 to 0.0 as it is in the wire and priced.
Rule 6 (disputed bar): revenue finding left capped at +0.3; GMV bar is the company guide, so not capped.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the closed placement funds logistics/JumiaPay and the CEO says breakeven does not need it; left at +0.3.
Scaled number: p_up moved from 45 to 46 (proxy evidence, sign agreeing with the run-up); print_vs_bar_pct softened from -3.0 to -2.5.
